item.title: In Limerence
item.description:
It’s never about them. It’s never about the other person. It’s about how we feel towards ourselves in their presence. In limerence, we try to work up the courage to say, “I love you.” When what we mean to say is, “I love myself when I’m with you.”

Humans are strange creatures; Their hearts possess the unique ability to turn scars into flowers, flowers which only bloom in the light of another. In isolation, We see only our wounds and scars. In limerence, The presence of another lets us see our flowers bloom And the colors make us feel worthy of our own love.

item.title: Elder Dragon
item.description:
I think deep down every dragon wants to be slain. Defeated, at least. They want to lay eyes on their Conquerer, and know it took someone formidible To vanquish them. And, in that, They know that they were great.

Deep down every dragon wants their name forever claimed By someone mighty. That’s why some are slain in battle, And others develop beer bellies and their own imprints on the sofa.

item.title: Numbers and Words
item.description:
Numbers were his first love, Words came later.

People often ran from Numbers; not appreciating their complexity. But he loved their nuance: adding, subtracting, dividing, multiplying; He’d watch them shift into familiar and comforting patterns.

Workbooks grew repetitive but he found Numbers everywhere: Street addresses, license plates, menu prices, and more. He’d watch them dance and rearrange themselves to fall asleep at night.

Then one day Words arrived and became his new obsession…Why? Because Numbers came easy, but Words required coaxing. Finding the right Words demanded more from him.

item.title: The Rounded Glass Box
item.description:
Once upon a time, A Phoenix saw a throng gathered in a swamp; Curious, the Phoenix flew down to investigate. She discovered men, women, and children; all standing in line To see and converse with The Man in the Rounded Glass Box.

The Box was a strange attraction, so translucent and round; The Man inside even more strange, for he refused to ever leave it. A kind, helpful man: he bore the wisdom of a well-traveled soul, Yet he never spoke of what lives he’d led before. He would chat and give counsel, But all that truly mattered to him was that he stayed inside the Glass Box, For its what kept him safe, he claimed.
